column1: # lemma | pos | tgt | tgt2 | gender | ipa | etymon | note
# tgt   citation form: singular noun, infinitive verb, masculine
#       singular adjective, nominative singular for Latin/Old English.
# tgt2  plural for nouns, present participle for verbs. A blank tgt2 on
#       a noun means the English plural is never woven, which is the
#       correct outcome: weaving a singular target under an English
#       plural teaches a form that does not exist.
# Verbs are woven as infinitives. "he courir" is not grammatical French and is
# not meant to be: the reader is decoding a French word inside an English
# clause, and the infinitive is the form they will meet in a dictionary.
# Present participles are supplied so English "-ing" forms read naturally.
# One spelling is sometimes two words. mort is death, from Latin mors, and
# dead, from mortuus, and English Wiktionary gives the two separate
# etymologies. A memory card is keyed by the target, so the second is
# written with a homograph number, "mort²", and is a card of its own;
# nothing a reader sees prints the number. Death is the one written bare,
# though Wiktionary numbers dead first, because death already had the card.
